question.problem: In a right triangle $\triangle ABC,$ we have $AC = 9,$ $BC=13,$ and $m\angle A = \alpha.$ Given that $\overline{AB}$ is the hypotenuse of the triangle, find the value of $\alpha$ (rounded to one decimal place).
question.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the triangle that's described.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14209655/assets/29ab71a468b9a57842e07ef74b8d8d770c7ebfacabb3735694c0dd40303ad220.png)

Since we are given the lengths of the adjacent and opposite sides, we can use tangent to find the angle measurement. We have

$$
\tan \alpha=  \dfrac{\textrm{opposite}}{\textrm{adjacent}}  = \dfrac{13}{9}.
$$

We now calculate $\alpha$ using the inverse tangent:

$$
\eqalign{
		\tan \alpha &= \dfrac{13}{9}\[5pt]
		\arctan( \tan \alpha) &= \arctan\left(\dfrac{13}{9} \right)\[5pt]
		\alpha &= \arctan\left(\dfrac{13}{9} \right)\[5pt]
&=(55.304\,8...)^\circ\[5pt]	
		 &\approx 55.3^\circ
	}
$$

rounded to one decimal place.
